title: Introduction to ESP32
subject: ECE / CPE
description: Learn the ESP32 development board, processor, memory, GPIO, wireless features, and a safe first LED program.
learningObjectives: Describe the ESP32 and its development board
Explain CPU, memory, GPIO, and digital input/output
Distinguish Wi-Fi and Bluetooth use cases
Prepare Arduino IDE and reason through a safe LED circuit

pages.title: What is ESP32?
pages.content:
The ESP32 is a family of microcontrollers from Espressif Systems. A microcontroller is a compact computer designed to run a focused program and interact directly with hardware.

ESP32 devices combine processing, memory, timers, communication peripherals, and integrated wireless radios. This makes them useful for sensor nodes, automation, connected controls, data logging, and rapid prototypes.

Microcontroller, not desktop computer: An ESP32 normally runs one embedded application repeatedly rather than a full desktop operating system.

pages.title: ESP32 Development Board
pages.content:
The ESP32 chip or module is commonly mounted on a development board. The board makes power, programming, reset, and pin access easier during prototyping.

USB connector
USB-to-serial interface
Voltage regulator
ESP32 module
GPIO headers

Common board features

  • A USB connector for power and data
  • Reset and boot buttons
  • A 3.3 V voltage regulator
  • Header pins labeled with GPIO numbers
  • One or more status LEDs

Board layouts vary. Always use the pinout and schematic for the exact model in front of you.

pages.title: CPU and Memory
pages.content:
The CPU executes program instructions. Depending on the ESP32 variant, the device may contain one or more processor cores and hardware features for real-time embedded work.

ResourceRoleWhat it holds
Flash memoryNon-volatile storageProgram code and saved data
RAMWorking memoryVariables, buffers, and active program state
ROMBuilt-in codeLow-level startup and boot support

Flash keeps its contents when power is removed. RAM is faster working space but loses its current contents when the board powers off.

pages.title: GPIO Pins
pages.content:
GPIO means General-Purpose Input/Output. Software can configure a supported pin as a digital input, digital output, or signal for a peripheral.

Pin capabilities vary

Some GPIOs can also support analog input, PWM, touch sensing, UART, SPI, or I2C. Other pins may be connected to onboard flash or influence how the chip boots.

Electrical limit: ESP32 GPIO normally uses 3.3 V logic and is not generally 5 V tolerant. Check the exact board documentation before applying a voltage.

pages.title: Digital Input and Output
pages.content:
A digital signal is interpreted as one of two states: LOW or HIGH. The voltage ranges that count as each state come from the device's electrical specifications.

ModeDirectionExample
Digital inputSignal enters ESP32Read a push button or digital sensor
Digital outputSignal leaves ESP32Control an LED or transistor

In Arduino-style code, pinMode() configures a pin, digitalRead() reads a state, and digitalWrite() sets an output HIGH or LOW.

pages.title: Wi-Fi
pages.content:
Built-in Wi-Fi lets an ESP32 communicate through an IP network. A project can join an existing access point, create its own access point, or combine both modes when supported.

Typical uses

  • Send sensor readings to an HTTP or MQTT service
  • Receive commands from a local dashboard
  • Serve a small configuration page
  • Synchronize time from a network source
Security habit: Do not hard-code real production passwords in a public repository. Use a local configuration process appropriate for the final project.

pages.title: Bluetooth
pages.content:
Bluetooth supports short-range communication with phones, computers, sensors, and other embedded devices. Supported capabilities depend on the exact ESP32 variant.

ApproachStrengthExample
Bluetooth ClassicContinuous device links and legacy profilesSerial-style data on supported variants
Bluetooth Low EnergyLow-power, small data exchangesSensor status or phone configuration

Bluetooth Low Energy organizes data into services and characteristics. A client can discover, read, write, or subscribe to those characteristics.

pages.title: Arduino IDE
pages.content:
Arduino IDE provides an editor, compiler workflow, board configuration, serial monitor, and uploader suitable for a first ESP32 project.

  1. Install the current Arduino IDE from its official source.
  2. Add Espressif ESP32 board support using the Boards Manager instructions.
  3. Connect a data-capable USB cable.
  4. Select the exact board model and serial port.
  5. Verify the sketch, then upload it.

If the board receives power but no port appears, test with a known data cable. Many charge-only cables omit the conductors required for USB communication.

pages.title: Basic LED Example
pages.content:
This sketch configures a GPIO as an output and alternates it between HIGH and LOW. Use the LED pin specified for your exact board.

const int ledPin = 2;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
  delay(500);
  digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);
  delay(500);
}

Before applying power

  • Confirm the selected GPIO is safe for output.
  • Check LED polarity.
  • Place a suitable current-limiting resistor in series.
  • Connect the circuit ground to the ESP32 ground.

pages.title: IoT Applications
pages.content:
IoT systems combine sensing, local decisions, communication, and an action or useful record. The ESP32 can handle several of these roles in one small device.

Environmental monitor

Read temperature and humidity, show a local status, and periodically send measurements.

Smart control

Read a switch or network command and safely control a relay interface.

Asset beacon

Advertise a short Bluetooth Low Energy identifier for nearby scanning.

Classroom data logger

Collect sensor readings and export them for later analysis.

A responsible design also considers power, network failure, data privacy, electrical safety, and what the device should do when a sensor produces an impossible value.

pages.title: Lesson Summary
pages.content:
You built a foundation for working with the ESP32 platform.

Key concepts

  • A development board makes the ESP32 easier to power, program, and connect.
  • Flash stores code while RAM holds active program data.
  • GPIO pins connect software to digital and peripheral signals.
  • Wi-Fi supports IP networking; Bluetooth supports nearby device communication.
  • Arduino IDE can compile and upload beginner ESP32 sketches.
  • A safe LED circuit uses the correct GPIO, polarity, ground, and current-limiting resistor.
Remember: Board variants differ. Confirm the exact pinout and voltage limits before wiring.

Suggested next action: Download the lesson, complete the reviewer, and plan the LED activity before taking the quiz.
